channel.title: Signal in the Scan
channel.description: A weekly peer-level digest of the most important new research on AI in medicine, focused on obstetrics and gynecology and on medical imaging, with Juno and Caspar.
channel.itunes:author: Juno & Caspar

item.title: Validation Rigor Separates Signal From Noise
item.description:
ESCAPE-MeVO reported. Thrombectomy versus medical management in medium-vessel occlusion — the trial answered whether the procedure works. Ospel and colleagues have now gone back into the imaging and asked the harder question: can baseline CT, CTA, and perfusion characteristics tell us who it works for? Which is where the next thrombectomy expansion argument lands. MeVO is already at the edge of what the evidence supports, and if imaging can stratify benefit, the...

item.title: Ultrasound Holds When PET Is Far Away
item.description:
This week's lead paper answers a staging question most of us have been settling by assumption. Frühauf and colleagues ran a prospective multicenter trial — the CANNES trial — and ultrasound came out non-inferior to PET/CT and DW-MRI for pelvic lymph node staging in cervical cancer. That's the finding. The conditions under which it holds are what we need to work through. "Non-inferior" is doing real work in that sentence. The design earns it — this isn't a soft r...

  1. 0:00 — Cold Open: What Changed This Week
  2. 0:02 — Headline: Citation and Design
  3. 0:03 — Headline: Effect and Numbers

  • Prospective comparison of diagnostic accuracy of ultrasound, PET/CT and DW-MRI for preoperative assessment of pelvic lymph nodes in cervical cancer patients: results of the CANNES trial - First prospective multicenter trial demonstrating ultrasound non-inferiority to PET/CT and DW-MRI for pelvic node staging in cervical cancer — directly informs resource allocation and staging protocols
  • Externally Tested AI Models for Malignancy Classification of Lung Nodules at Chest CT: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis - Provides pooled external validation benchmarks for AI lung nodule classifiers — essential for understanding real-world performance expectations

  • Evaluating Accuracy of LI-RADS Nonradiation Treatment Response Algorithm v2024 and Ancillary Features at Hepatobiliary MRI versus CT - Confirms updated LI-RADS TRA v2024 with ancillary features improves HCC viability assessment — relevant for structured reporting algorithm evolution

item.title: Annotation Light, Validation Heavy
item.description:
This week's lead paper is a methods story, not a clinical one. ProViCNet demonstrates consistent multicenter detection on prostate MRI without lesion-level annotation. If it holds in prospective validation, it changes what's feasible to build — not what's deployable today. So the news is upstream of practice. For now, yes.   2. 0:49 — Headline: Citation, Design, and the Choice That Earns the Evidence Grade
  3. 1:37 — Headline: Numbers, Heterogeneity, and What "Six Cohorts" Does and Doesn't Prove
  4. 2:26 — Headline: Practice Impact — Honest About "Nothing Yet"

  9. 6:29 — Close: What to Watch, What's Unsettled, Sign-Off


Follow-up links:
  • Enhancing foundation model transfer for prostate cancer detection with patch-level contrastive learning - Demonstrates that weakly supervised contrastive learning can maintain consistent prostate cancer detection across six heterogeneous MRI cohorts without pixel-level annotation
  • Deep learning for H&E-based meningioma molecular classification and outcome prediction - Shows that routine histology slides can predict meningioma molecular subtypes and recurrence, potentially reducing reliance on genomic testing
  • One-year follow-up after US-guided transperineal focal laser ablation of localized prostate cancer - Provides multicenter registry data on 12-month oncological outcomes for image-guided focal therapy, informing patient selection discussions

item.title: Matching the Tumor Board
item.description:
Before this week, every multimodal AI paper in gyn-onc imaging was benchmarked against individual radiologists or single-center reads. Yu and colleagues used MDT consensus — tumor board agreement across gyn-onc, radiology, and pathology — as the reference standard, and validated externally across multiple centers. That's the bar that actually matters for clinical translation, and this week it got cleared. With the caveat that MDT consensus is imperfect ground t...

Juno, Caspar, and any guest voices are AI-generated. Episode text and audio are generated with human-directed software.

Chapters:
  1. 0:00 — Cold Open: The Benchmark Shift
  2. 0:57 — Headline: Clinical Question and Study Design
  3. 1:55 — Headline: Effect Size and What Parity Means
  4. 2:52 — Headline: Practice Impact and Honest Limits
  5. 3:50 — Round 1: HCC Contrast Agent Equivalence (Heo)
  6. 4:47 — Round 2: Pancreatic Cancer Detection on CT (Yamaguchi)
  7. 5:45 — Round 3: Air Pollution and Coronary Risk, Sex-Specific (Castillo)
  8. 6:42 — Round 4: Net Water Uptake for Thrombectomy Selection (Lakhani)
  9. 7:40 — Close: What to Watch, What's Still Unsettled


Follow-up links:
  • Integrating ultrasound-CT-MR for preoperative multi-task prediction in ovarian cancer: achieving diagnostic parity with multidisciplinary team consensus - First large external validation showing multimodal AI matches MDT consensus across five preoperative ovarian cancer classification tasks — a credible benchmark for clinical translation in gyn-onc.
  • Diagnostic Accuracy of Extracellular versus Hepatobiliary Contrast-enhanced MRI in LI-RADS Nonradiation Treatment Response Algorithm Version 2024 - Demonstrates equivalent accuracy between ECA-MRI and HBA-MRI for post-treatment HCC assessment, informing protocol flexibility in surveillance imaging.
  • Deep Learning Detection of Direct and Indirect Imaging Findings Associated with Pancreatic Cancer at Contrast-enhanced and Noncontrast CT - Multiinstitutional DL model detects pancreatic cancer on both NCCT and CECT with physician-level performance, opening doors for opportunistic screening.
  • Sex-Specific Associations between Long-term Air Pollution Exposure and Coronary Atherosclerosis at Cardiac CT - Large cohort data linking PM2.5 and NO2 to coronary plaque burden with sex-specific patterns — relevant for cardiovascular risk counseling.
  • Ischemic Lesion Net Water Uptake Outperforms ASPECTS and CBF Less Than 30% in Predicting Futile Recanalization after Mechanical Thrombectomy - Net water uptake emerges as a superior imaging biomarker for thrombectomy patient selection, potentially reducing futile interventions.

item.title: When MRI Met the Molecular Classifier
item.description:
FIGO 2023 added three molecular classifiers to endometrial cancer staging — POLE mutation status, mismatch repair deficiency, p53 abnormality. Each carries independent prognostic weight. None of them show up on MRI. If your preoperative workflow hasn't been updated since the new staging came in, you're running imaging reports against a system that requires data your scanner can't provide. Avesani and colleagues measured what that gap actually costs in concorda...

Juno, Caspar, and any guest voices are AI-generated. Episode text and audio are generated with human-directed software.

Chapters:
  1. 0:00 — Cold Open: The Structural Problem
  2. 0:51 — Headline: Design and Population
  3. 1:41 — Headline: The Finding and the Definitional Caveat
  4. 2:32 — Headline: Practice Implication
  5. 3:22 — Pivot and Round 1: Kitaguchi (AI Surgical Overlay)
  6. 4:13 — Round 2: Abiodun-Ojo (PSMA-11 vs Fluciclovine)
  7. 5:03 — Round 3: Ranieri Guimaraes (SCOT-HEART Body Composition)
  8. 5:54 — Round 4: Shin (H&E Neoadjuvant Response Prediction)
  9. 6:44 — Close: What to Watch, What Is Unsettled


Follow-up links:
  • Pelvic MRI in Endometrial Cancer Staging: A Retrospective Evaluation of the Impact of FIGO 2023 - Demonstrates that FIGO 2023 molecular criteria reduce MRI-pathology concordance, forcing a rethink of preoperative imaging workflows in endometrial cancer.
  • Enhancing anatomical recognition by surgeons during pelvic lymph node dissection using artificial intelligence - Shows AI overlay can meaningfully improve intraoperative anatomical identification, with implications for reducing surgical complications in pelvic oncology.
  • 18F-Fluciclovine or 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT-guided Salvage Radiotherapy Changes in Postprostatectomy Biochemical Recurrence: Secondary Analysis of the EMPIRE-2 Trial - RCT-derived evidence that PSMA-11 PET/CT changes salvage RT planning more than fluciclovine, informing tracer selection in recurrent prostate cancer.
  • Machine Learning Multiorgan Analysis of Coronary CT Angiography Body Composition, Myocardial Infarction, and Mortality in the SCOT-HEART Trial - Demonstrates that ML-extracted body composition from routine coronary CTA adds independent prognostic value for hard cardiovascular endpoints over 10 years.
  • Predicting response to neoadjuvant therapy using artificial intelligence on digitized histopathology slides: a systematic review - Synthesizes the state of AI for neoadjuvant response prediction, highlighting promising accuracy but critical gaps in external validation and standardization.

item.title: The Hyperdense Capsule's Verdict
item.description:
MMA embolization for nonacute subdural hematoma has been picking up procedural volume at most centers for several years. The selection criteria haven't kept pace with that. We've been applying the procedure broadly without a reliable way to identify who actually benefits. Some fraction of those patients are absorbing procedural risk for no expected gain. That's the specific problem. Weng and colleagues may have found a way to resolve it — using a fea...

  1. 0:00 — Cold Open: The Selection Problem
  2. 0:57 — Headline: Citation and Design
  3. 1:55 — Headline: The Finding and the Caveat
  4. 2:52 — Headline: Practice Implication
  5. 3:49 — Round 1: Cardiac MRI Entropy in Myocarditis (Wang)
  6. 4:47 — Round 2: Noncontrast Abbreviated MRI for HCC Post-TACE (Jeon)

  8. 6:42 — Round 4: RECIBM Bone Metastasis Response Criteria (Xu, Radiology)
  9. 7:39 — Close: What to Watch, What's Unsettled


Follow-up links:
  • Hyperdense Capsule Sign at Noncontrast CT as an Indication for Middle Meningeal Artery Embolization for Nonacute Subdural Hematomas: A MAGIC-MT Trial Post Hoc Analysis - Identifies an imaging biomarker that may stratify which SDH patients benefit from MMA embolization, potentially rationalizing procedural selection.
  • Entropy for Prediction of MACEs in Myocarditis: A Cardiac MRI-based Biomarker of Myocardial Tissue Heterogeneity - Adds a texture-based prognostic metric to cardiac MRI in myocarditis, independent of LGE and EF.
  • Noncontrast Abbreviated MRI for Post-TACE Treatment Response Monitoring of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Based on Ancillary Features from LI-RADS - Explores a contrast-sparing surveillance option for HCC patients post-TACE, relevant for renal-impaired or high-frequency imaging populations.
  • Prediction of incident atrial fibrillation from retinal fundus images using a multimodal foundation model - Demonstrates that retinal imaging encodes AF risk, validated across multiethnic cohorts, with potential for opportunistic screening.
  • Response Evaluation Criteria in Bone Metastases: Performance and Association of Response Classifications with Survival Outcomes - Proposes new bone metastasis response criteria with stronger survival association than existing frameworks, addressing a gap in oncologic imaging.

item.title: When AI Redirects the Reader's Eye
item.description:
Chen and colleagues this week asked whether you can predict platinum response in ovarian cancer before you start treatment — not from a single biomarker, but from transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data fused together. AUC 0.939. Retrospective design. Both of those things are true simultaneously, and that's where we're starting. The other paper worth flagging before we get there — Taib, in Radiology — actually has the higher importance score. Eye-tracking dat...

Juno, Caspar, and any guest voices are AI-generated. Episode text and audio are generated with human-directed software.

Chapters:
  1. 0:00 — Cold Open: What This Week Changes
  2. 0:59 — Headline: Clinical Question and Design Choice
  3. 1:58 — Headline: Effect Size and Its Conditions
  4. 2:57 — Headline: Practice Impact and Open Thread
  5. 3:56 — Pivot and Round 1: Taib Mammography / Automation Bias
  6. 4:55 — Round 2: Lin CXR Foundation Model
  7. 5:54 — Round 3: Kim PROVISION-AF / AI-ECG in Atrial Fibrillation
  8. 6:53 — Round 4: Chen ccRCC / H&E-Based Immunotherapy Prediction
  9. 7:52 — Close: What to Watch, What's Unsettled


Follow-up links:
  • Multi-omics fusion with machine learning enables robust prediction of treatment response in ovarian cancer for precision population health. - First multi-omics fusion model for ovarian cancer chemotherapy response with AUC 0.939; identifies novel chemoresistance drivers; needs prospective validation.
  • Automation Bias in Action: Eye Tracking of Humans Reading Screening Mammograms with and without AI Prompts. - Eye-tracking evidence that incorrect AI prompts cause readers to miss cancers and over-call false positives; directly relevant to breast imaging workflow design.
  • Transparent chest radiograph foundation model enables explainable human disease profiling. - Foundation model predicts over 1,000 phenotypes from CXR across three cohorts; demonstrates systemic disease profiling potential with explainability.
  • Impact of an AI algorithm for multi-day prediction of incident atrial fibrillation on clinical decision-making: PROVISION-AF study. - Multinational simulation shows AI-ECG improves physician AF prediction from AUROC 0.57 to 0.65; modest but real decision-support benefit.
  • Deep learning-based CD8+ T cell model for predicting prognosis and targeted immunotherapy benefit in ccRCC. - H&E-based deep learning infers CD8+ inflammation and predicts immunotherapy benefit in renal cell carcinoma; AUC ~0.78 across two multicenter cohorts.
